Report_ID: Participants with symptomatic, culture-verified urinary tract infection (urinary E. coli positive) at 90 days
Title: A Randomized, Double Blind, Controlled, Dose Dependent Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy of a Proanthocyanidin Standardized Whole Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) Powder on Infections of the Urinary Tract
Author: Sengupta, K.; Alluri, K.V.; Golakoti, T.; Gottumukkala, G.V.; Raavi, J.; Kotchrlakota, L.; Sigalan, S.C.; Dey, D.; Ghosh, S.; Chatterjee, A.
Comment: No between-group effect size, test statistic or p-value for the treatment-vs-control UTI comparison is reported by the paper; only event counts are extracted. Analysed sample (n=57) used because 3 control participants dropped out immediately after randomization (ITT counts not reported). Baseline E. coli positivity was markedly imbalanced (control 30.8% vs 66.7%/74% in cranberry arms), so the 90-day between-group risk ratio is confounded. Control arm was untreated (no placebo).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('PS-WCP cranberry powder (500 mg/day + 1000 mg/day combined)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: urology / nutraceutical prevention of recurrent urinary tract infection
Content length: 90 days of supplementation with evaluations at baseline, day 10, 30, 60 and 90
Topic of Content: Proanthocyanidin-standardized whole cranberry powder (PS-WCP) for prevention of recurrent UTI
Participant type: Women aged 18-40 years with a history of recurrent UTIs, currently culture positive with mild UTI symptoms
Recruitment source: Clinical trial site at Eluru, Andhra Pradesh, India (ASRAM); 225 female patients assessed, 60 enrolled
Outcome measurement: Number (and percentage) of subjects positive for urinary E. coli at the 90-day evaluation, out of subjects analysed per group; cranberry arms (500 mg/day and 1000 mg/day) combined per synthesis plan (9+6=15 of 21+23=44)
Outcome variable: Participants with symptomatic, culture-verified urinary tract infection (urinary E. coli positive) at 90 days
additional_group_ns: Reported separately in Table 4 as two cranberry arms: PS-WCP 500 mg/day n=21 (9 E. coli positive at 90 days, 42.8%) and PS-WCP 1000 mg/day n=23 (6 E. coli positive at 90 days, 26.1%); summed into one cranberry group per synthesis plan. 60 randomized (control n=16), 3 control dropouts, analysed sample n=57 used (not ITT).
effect_direction: favours cranberry (15/44 = 34.1% vs 5/13 = 38.5%; RR ≈ 0.89, not significant)
